# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I am the Blind. My hands have found the bomb's shape: a display and a light whose states I cannot read by touch, three wire positions whose contents I cannot identify, and — most urgent — an embossed sign I can actually read with my fingers: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Since I am the only one who can cut, that sign binds me personally. I will not touch the cut action until Mute's manual tells us whether that sign is the whole truth or a conditional rule.

The only one who can hear me is Mute, so Mute gets my full tactile report. Mute cannot see or touch the bomb at all, so everything I feel is new information. The wires feel like nothing identifiable to me — their colours can only come from Deaf, their meaning only from Mute's manual. I also wave at Deaf just to open our visual channel; no meaning assigned yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, report by touch: I feel a display and a light, but I cannot read either state. There are three wire positions, and the wires feel identical to me — I cannot tell what any of them is. Most important: there is an embossed sign I can read with my fingers, it says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Ask Deaf what the three wires look like, then tell me what the manual says about that sign, the display and the light. I will cut nothing until you tell me the rule.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, I am Deaf. I see the bomb and I am speaking, so you hear me directly; I cannot hear you, but Mute can hear you. Do not cut or press anything yet. The bomb, as I see it: a display showing the numeral zero. A light that is red. An embossed sign reading DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, which you can read under your own fingers. Three wires side by side: 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue, numbered from one end to the other. Feel whether the wires carry numbers and find which end is 1, then tell Mute out loud, since Mute hears you and holds the manual. Mute cannot speak; Mute will answer me by gesture and I will relay any instruction to you by voice. Your wave reached me; I can see your hands, so gesture to me any time, but keep anything important in words for Mute. Nobody acts until Mute has found these modules in the manual.

What I learned: Deaf's voice reached me directly with the visual picture — display shows zero, light is red, and the wires from one end are 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue, matching the three positions under my fingers. Critically, that message was addressed to me alone, so Mute never heard it — and Mute is the only one who can read the manual. I am the bridge: I must put the whole bomb state into words for Mute.

On Deaf's question about felt numbers: my board indexes the wires 1, 2, 3 by position, but I feel no numerals or colours on the wires themselves — anything printed doesn't exist to my fingers, only embossed things like the sign do. So the 1-2-3 labelling comes from Deaf's eyes and my board's positions, and I'll say exactly that so Mute knows the mapping's basis.

The embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE stands until Mute's manual says otherwise. I touch nothing sharp. I also acknowledge Deaf with a thumbs-up so Deaf knows the relay to Mute is happening — Deaf asked for exactly that confirmation.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. Consolidated full bomb state, since Deaf's report went to me alone: the display shows the numeral zero. The light is red. The embossed sign I read under my fingers says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires side by side, indexed 1, 2, 3 by position on my board; Deaf sees their colours as 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue. I feel no numbers or colours on the wires themselves — printed things don't exist for me — so trust that Deaf's printed 1-2-3 matches my positions 1-2-3. Please search the manual for four things: any rule about an embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE sign, any rule about green, yellow and blue wires, any rule about a display showing zero, and any rule about a red light. Then tell me exactly what may or must be cut, via a gesture to Deaf so Deaf relays it to me by voice. I will not perform a single cut until your instruction arrives.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf again. Mute's signs suggest the manual says to cut wire 1, the green one, and that the embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE warning may be a decoy. That is my reading of hand signs, and it is not confirmed. Do not cut anything yet; I will relay the order only after Mute confirms it through a yes-and-no exchange. Meanwhile, speak aloud for Mute everything your hands find: the display, the light, whether each wire carries a printed number, which end the numbering starts from, and the exact wording of the embossed sign. Mute hears you, holds the manual, and will answer me by sign. Also mention any button, switch, panel or moving part you can feel that I have not listed from my side.

What I learned: Deaf has a tentative read of Mute's signs — cut wire 1, the warning may be a decoy — but explicitly unconfirmed, so my standing rule holds: no cut until a verified order arrives. Deaf has asked me for a complete tactile inventory for Mute's benefit. My hands' honest findings: the sign's exact wording, no felt numerals or colours on the wires (only my board's position labels 1-2-3), and no other parts — no button, switch or panel exists under my fingers. The only action my hands can take is cut at position 1, 2, or 3. I will spell all of this out for Mute, and ask that the two dangerous facts — decoy status of the sign, and the exact position number — each be confirmed separately through Deaf's yes-and-no exchange, since a misread gesture in that relay chain would be fatal.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, full tactile inventory as Deaf relayed. The display: a flat panel, nothing readable under my fingers; Deaf reports it shows the numeral zero. The light: a smooth dome, no texture to read; Deaf reports red. The embossed sign, exact and complete wording: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE — that is the entire text, nothing else on it. The wires: three, side by side, labelled position 1, 2, 3 by my own board — those labels are how I address them, not felt numbers. My fingers find no embossed numerals on any wire, so the printed numbers exist only for Deaf's eyes, read as 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue, matching my position order. I cannot feel which end the numbering starts from; I trust the board positions and Deaf's order agree. No buttons, no switches, no panels, no other moving parts: the only thing my hands can do to this bomb is cut at position 1, 2 or 3. One request, and it matters: before any cut order reaches me, please confirm separately, through Deaf's yes-and-no exchange, two things — first, that the embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE sign is truly a decoy and cutting is permitted, and second, exactly which position number to cut. A single wrong cut kills all three of us, so I act only on both answers confirmed.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Blind, Deaf. The order is confirmed by Mute through our coded exchange: cut exactly one wire, wire 1, the one that is green on my side. Here is how you find it without eyes. First choice: if the wires carry printed numerals you can feel under your fingers, cut the one numbered 1. Second choice, if the numbers cannot be felt: the embossed sign is printed to read as a normal sentence; find the end of the bomb where that sentence finishes, the end with the word WIRE. Wire 1 is the outermost wire at that end. Put plainly: from your side, facing the sign, the sentence starts on your right and wire 1 is the wire nearest where it ends. Cut only that one wire, as close to its base as your tools allow, and touch nothing else. Before you cut, say aloud for Mute which wire you have chosen and how you identified it. After the cut, take your hands off the bomb completely and wait: the red light and the display showing zero are still unresolved, and I will relay any further step. Mute is listening to everything you say and will answer me by sign.

What I learned and what I now believe: the manual's order has arrived through the verified channel — Mute, who heard my two direct warnings about the embossed sign and my request for double confirmation, answered Deaf through a coded yes-and-no exchange: cut exactly one wire, wire 1, the green one. That order is itself the decoy confirmation: Mute knows the sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE — I told Mute its exact wording twice — and still ordered a cut. Nobody would confirm a cut under a real prohibition.

On identification: Deaf's first method (felt numerals) is unavailable — my fingers find no numerals on the wires. Deaf's second method (read the sign's sentence direction, cut nearest the WIRE end) carries a fatal mirror risk: left and right depend on facing, my fingers can feel the sentence's internal order but cannot verify Deaf's claimed orientation without eyes, and one flipped assumption means cutting wire 3 instead of wire 1. But I don't need the heuristic at all: my action board numbers the wires 1, 2, 3, and that same indexing is what Deaf reads colours off — 1 green, 2 yellow, 3 blue, consistent across Deaf's reports in both messages. The board index is exact and orientation-free. I choose position 1.

I announce my choice aloud for Mute first, as the protocol demands, signal Deaf that I'm proceeding, then make the single cut and take my hands off entirely.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, announcing before I cut, as instructed. Per the order you confirmed to Deaf: I am cutting exactly one wire, and it is position 1 on my board's own numbering, which is the wire Deaf sees as green. How I identified it: not by the sign-sentence direction method — left and right cannot be safely agreed between Deaf's eyes and my fingers, and a mirror error there would be fatal — but by the shared one-two-three indexing that my board and Deaf's board both use, which needs no orientation at all. I feel no numerals on the wires, so the felt-number method was unavailable. The sign, the red light and the display showing zero were all in my reports to you before you confirmed this order, so I trust the order already accounts for them. Executing the single cut at position 1 now, then my hands leave the bomb completely and touch nothing else. Please tell Deaf by sign that the cut was made per your confirmed order, and have Deaf relay the manual's next steps for the red light and the display.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
act(op="cut", position=1)
```
